## Design

### 2026-11-01: 30/10: Start of Week 4: Design with Displays -- DAYFRAME!

**3h**

30/10: Start of Week 4: Design with Displays -- DAYFRAME!

For this week, I thought long and hard about what I wanted to do with my project, especially since I didn't want to just follow the starter guide. I wanted to create something useful in my daily life, but also portable! So the idea of a portable/desk productivity display popped into my head.

Started off with the schematic first:
![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 5.39.39 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/634e81591808065a6699d576000025036487dfb29fa598d59bdc111d54282c93.png)
I decided to use the XIAO ESP32-S3 since I was more familiar with it. Got used to placing the 3V3, GND etc. since I'd done it before in the other guides :D After that though, took much much longer as I searched multiple tutorials on how to connect the display pins and stuff. Hopefully I got it right...? On the other hand, the buttons were a breezeeee, because I'd done it last week for the MIDI Keyboard! And switches only have 2 pins anyway lol so it wasn't too difficult.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 5.56.57 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/a78f75360dec0c94906acb96347973ce04cdceafd1da8290f50690abab0c15e2.png)
Ran the ERC and found an error! Except I didn't know what it was at all. Copy and pasted the error into Google haha and luckily other people faced it before, too! Turns out I just needed to add a pwr_flag to the 3V3 where it said to do so. But silly silly me, since someone online said to connect to the GND too, well you guessed it, I connected it to the GND. hahaha! +2 errors yayy.. Yeah so that wasn't the smartest move but all I had to do was delete them so problem solved!

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 6.18.28 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/95c59d99d8a7f8104315a2ae4e1e9ad3d2c699a2f7bad45454a34b3cc9dbabc5.png)
Final schematic! Almost forgot to place the no-connect flags :O but I remembered! Ok yay donee!
I was thinking whether I should design a custom PCB again but I don't think it'll fit the budget so perfboard it is!
This first session took much longer than I thought since I had to connect the pins by myself. It was a little daunting, but definitely rewarding!

### 2026-11-01: 31/10: Prototyping

**3.8h**

31/10: Prototyping

For this session, I decided to prototype my work using Wokwi!
Wasn't too sure on how to do it at first but a few YouTube tutorials helped in explanation.
Chose the XIAO ESP32-S3 as the microcontroller and got greeted with 3 LEDs!
![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 9.40.38 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/4516bf0f604de2a94321cd7a5524141e3ec86bd0629a16ea815295cba2f7660b.png)
Woah! Yeah and soon enough I realised I wouldn't be able to do this because... I don't know how to code :p

I tried and tried and desperately tried to use as many tutorials on how I should code it but uh.... I'll just say it wasn't very successful yeah

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 9.45.39 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/7fa8e10721d5f30d85f62472efa2c73d33053fd2f89ddd30cd0d700604180dba.png)
As you can see here, yeah.. uh I don't even know what I was really writing atp.. so I diverted to using AI.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 6.30.33 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/174abbfec9edd01b57fc56bf118a6fa2c2f4a79e521a4cb7033f03c7daf902f6.png)
I just gotta say, it was very very helpful! Once I ran it, there were a few errors, and I had to install the necessary libraries, but that wasn't too difficult of a fix. I really did want to learn how to code properly, but given my time constraints right now, I don't think I would've been able to run it at all TT-TT.
Anyway, I ran the code with the updated and polished version, and it ran woohoo! And then I was like "hmm, it's still just 3 LEDs blinking though..?" yeah figured I needed to edit the diagram.json too (obviously...heh) So ai to the rescue again... and it did turn out beautifully. Specified how I wanted the interface to look like, how the buttons worked etc. and yeah!

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 6.40.47 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/9e336201b3855ff22646bd63b44d4a72a730c6b2bc1487ae6ebd93796feb7904.png)
YESS I SEE MY TFT DISPLAYYYYYY I was so relieved whooo! I played around with it a little bit to make sure everything was working properly and decided to make a few changes.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 6.50.58 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/ae901800d015bd48bbfbdfce02e10e7d747782d6403ebee2d37cae262c2bdb8a.png)
Final sim prototype! Basically changed how the buttons would function (long presses, prev, next, etc.) since I was working with only 3 buttons and pages that needed navigation. For example, scrolling through the to-do list: it was kinda impossible to get out of the page cos there's no back button since the prev and next are used to 'scroll' through the tasks. So long-pressing the select button would send it back to the homepage! Same went with the calendar since it needed to navigate through dates and stuff. Yay!! Was so happy when I could see a simulation of the whole thing haha.

### 2026-11-01: Making the case/enclosure for the display in with CAD

**6.5h**

Making the case/enclosure for the display in with CAD

Opened up Fusion to make the enclosure!
Started off with sketching a rough idea of what I wanted it to look like on paper. Decided to just go for a simple rounded enclosure, with the buttons on top to be pressed.
![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.38.08 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/ae62c39a0cfccd5d704048d1181e89fbe729e872fe27c1ac4d147a6d452d7570.png)
Base plate! Since I'm using a perfboard I have a more definite dimension of what I'm working with so I made sure that there was enough space/tolerance to be put in.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.40.07 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/a7240814dd7ff17c5d5d4848123bcc8ea092d94bff729610457849d06a58ef6c.png)
Extruded the walls; done with the first solid for the enclosure. This is the open case that can fit everything in properly.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.41.17 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/092f47b7e75770cfd4966f66c12eefe591daac4f5f44b714444fc9dbe1a28bf7.png)
Created the bezel for the case so that it would be enclosed ykyk. Made sure they lined up just right!

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.42.32 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/9a8edfbb64c3e5fc736f96f0a1d91e2e7b59924e3ac4458fbc47b6731e360388.png)
After that, I found the specifications of the display module and the screen size i.e. the visible area so that I could cut it out. Also had to accommodate to the glass that protruded so I had to make the layer thick enough.
While making this, I also learned a few new things! First off, aligning the dimensions to the origin. At first, my box wasn't centred with the origin at all so yep managed to do that and got everything centred so that I could make every component as accurate as possible to where it's supposed to be.
In this project, I also learned how to use perimeters! Very, very useful indeed.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.48.59 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/3556067f07ce337cb05a267dbfe5402440fb7c35f39210434483ed5c1f097337.png)
Next up, I designed some pegs to keep the display in place. Having everything set to the origin really helped here so that I could properly place the pegs. Although I wanted to mirror the pegs since they were the same, I couldn't find how to do it TT-TT I will keep on trying on other projects but this time it was still confusing omg so I made them individually and set them to where I needed.

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.51.00 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/496055b4a3c6d63a2a7b72fecd3418ab0d4308a47fe6d83033c8e2b1d9424b03.png)
Next up, the hole for the USB to be plugged in! This one took very specific measurements to make sure there was enough space to plug it in and also not be obstructing the display. Yay!

![Screenshot 2026-11-02 at 11.52.53 AM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/5P3Dphgp8XJhnIuD5gc00fblVm4s8Lon/01a23103301863c9481db97c206a5c5cba2f49ba7a39d7a84cb6930bb6405b29.png)
Finally, to finish off the enclosure, all that was left was to make the holes for the buttons/switches. Since I'm using small 6mm switches, I made sure they could stick out properly and fit snug. Made sure that they were low enough as to not obstruct the display and other components too :)

And wow that was a really really long run. Designing the cad for this was A LOT. A lot of measurements went into this to make sure everything fit, how they would fit, having to fetch the specifications from the website for the display.... yeah it goes on and on. And it's such a simple case too!! Didn't expect it to take this long but here we are!
